population.note: FICTIONAL. Based on about 274M adults. Current users: 28.6% ≈ 78.4M. Ever used: 40.5% ≈ 111M, up 5.0 points, inside the 6.6 limit. Used but off now: 11.9 points ≈ 32.6M. Never used: ≈163M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 40.5 − current 28.6 = 11.9 points off now. About 13.5 points of current users are on a second or later course, because $35 generics and monthly MariTide re-enrolled many lapsed users. About 4.3 points of the off-now group had restarted once and then stopped again. So (13.5+4.3)/40.5 ≈ 44% have cycled. Overall one-year persistence is up only slightly, from ~35% to ~40%. It runs at ~60% on clinic-administered monthly MariTide and stays at ~45–50% under gated plans. Age check: 18–29 15% × 52M = 7.8M; 30–49 31.2% × 91M = 28.4M; 50–64 42% × 62M = 26.0M; 65+ 23.5% × 69M = 16.2M; total 78.4M = 28.6%. The 65+ band rose from 17% to 23.5% for three reasons: generic semaglutide on a $10 Part D tier, the April 2034 tirzepatide cognitive-decline indication (≈1.1M Medicare starts in eight months, some with BMI too low for the obesity benefit), and fewer pauses as DEXA vans caught up. Even so, about one in six ever-users aged 65+ is off on a medically advised bone pause. The bottom third rose from 21% to 27%. Generics at $29–59 cash, eight more continuation-standard states and fewer imports explain it. The gap with the top third is now 3 points, against 7 in 2032. Who is off: (a) about 9M paused or dropped by gating; (b) about 6M stopped because of GI effects or the newly labelled 'grey'; (c) refusers by conviction, a group that grew in absolute number for the first time since 2029, concentrated among under-35s in Atlanta, Tulsa and the Dallas exurbs; (d) people with contraindications; (e) rural uninsured residents of the 11 non-adopting states, for whom $39 is still a monthly decision. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, mostly 12+ on generic semaglutide through Medicaid EPSDT. The adolescent bone-accrual full dataset was submitted in Nov 2034 and is unreviewed. About two children in five now live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Public programmes now pay more fills than commercial plans. Medicare: the permanent Part D obesity benefit is unchanged (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity, continuation standard, counselling visit). From Jan 2034 most Part D plans put generic semaglutide on a $10 preferred-generic tier at a net ≈$40/month. Branded agents stay at the $199 negotiated rate with a $50 copay. Tirzepatide's April 2034 cognitive-decline indication is a medically accepted indication, so Part D covers it outside the obesity benefit for adults 60+ with BMI ≥27 and a vascular risk factor. Medicare users ≈17.6M (16.2M aged 65+ plus ≈1.4M disabled under-65) = 22.4% of fills. Of these, ≈9.7M are on generic (9.7M × $40 × 12 ≈ $4.7B) and ≈7.9M on branded (7.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $18.9B), so gross ≈ $23.5B, below 2032's $30.6B despite 37% more users. Beneficiary copays: 9.7M × $10 × 12 ≈ $1.2B plus 7.9M × $50 × 12 ≈ $4.7B = $5.9B, leaving the programme ≈ $17.6B. Medicaid: 8 more states adopted the existing continuation standard for the 90% match once their 10% share fell to ≈$3.50 per user-month on generic. Georgia, Missouri, Tennessee and South Carolina are among them, making 39 states plus DC. Medicaid users ≈14.5M = 18.5% of fills: ≈10.9M generic × $35 × 12 ≈ $4.6B plus ≈3.6M branded × $199 × 12 ≈ $8.6B = ≈$13.2B gross. Public total ≈32.1M users = 40.9% of fills, against commercial 35.1%.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month and the first legal tirzepatide generics for domestic and African markets. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide, and Chinese API now also feeds US-approved generics. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 35–60. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics. Ex-US branded revenue keeps eroding.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic collapse for semaglutide only. Under the Sep 2031 settlements, six ANDA generics and a Novo authorised generic launched in March 2033. By mid-2034 generic injectable semaglutide costs $29–59/month cash (median ≈$39), and generic liraglutide ≈$25. Generic oral semaglutide is not yet in the US. Tirzepatide, retatrutide, amycretin, MariTide and Foundayo remain branded. Branded prices: Zepbound vials $179–249 direct (Lilly trimmed them after generic entry), retatrutide $399 direct and $1,499 list, MariTide $349 direct, amycretin $449, Foundayo $149. Payer mix of ≈78.4M users: Medicare 17.6M (22.4%), Medicaid 14.5M (18.5%), commercial 27.5M (35.1%; ≈6.0M of them on generic), cash/direct 16.0M (20.4%; ≈4.5M generic, including ≈2.6M of the ≈4.6M 'calm' subscribers on microdose generic injectable, with the other ≈2.0M on Foundayo), imported/counterfeit 2.8M (3.6%). Sum 78.4M = 100%. US market ≈ $119B: ≈31.1M generic users × $40 × 12 ≈ $14.9B plus ≈44.5M branded users × ≈$195 net × 12 ≈ $104.1B, down from $145B with 18% more users. Generic entry did not reach the drugs the affluent and the cognition-indicated older users want most. Around 70% of covering employers still use gated designs, and many now steer to generic first. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg, and US generics from Mar 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance; allocation lifted Aug 2033)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide, approved Jun 2033)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Mar 2033)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda and generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction in risk of cognitive decline in adults 60+ with overweight/obesity and vascular risk (tirzepatide, Apr 2034); limitation of use: not shown to treat Alzheimer's disease
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'even' subscriptions (≈4.6M subscribers; microdose generic semaglutide at $59–89 or Foundayo at $149), now required to carry the anhedonia statement
generic semaglutide 'for the brain' in under-60s and in people without vascular risk, which the indication does not cover
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial still enrolling)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Monthly_or_implant is met by MariTide. Under review at the start, it was approved in Jun 2033 on 72-week DEXA data with a mean loss of ~17–20% and body-composition monitoring in the label. It can be self-injected but is usually given in a clinic or at on-site employer injection days. ≈2.6M users by end 2034 after a supply-limited ramp. No implant is on the US market. A six-month subdermal incretin depot is in phase 2 and is not available. Survodutide was approved in Mar 2033 for chronic weight management (weekly), and its MASH supplement was filed. Bimagrumab + semaglutide filed in Mar 2034 as the first lean-mass-sparing combination, so approval cannot come before 2035. Cognition_dementia comes from SURMOUNT-COG (fictional; started 2029): 9,400 adults aged 60–80, BMI ≥27, ≥1 vascular risk factor, 4 years. The composite of incident MCI or dementia was 9.8% versus 12.4% on placebo (HR 0.79). The indication was approved Apr 2034 as risk reduction, with an explicit limitation, because semaglutide's 2025 EVOKE trials in early Alzheimer's disease had failed. Tirzepatide exclusivity keeps this indication branded. Incretin market ≈ $141B in 2034: US ≈ $119B, ex-US ≈ $22B.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. MariTide's first-dose nausea is notable, and clinics now titrate it down.
Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ population and high-dose retatrutide.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Fewer counterfeit confounders now that imports are down.

With 16.2M users aged 65+, a 2034 Medicare claims update estimates ≈1.8M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria. Cognition-indicated tirzepatide users are often lighter at baseline, which worries geriatricians.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and MariTide labels. The CMS annual DEXA rule is unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.0M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip fracture × 0.35 excess ≈ 16,800 excess hip fractures a year against ~305,000 US total, partly offset by antiresorptive co-prescription. DEXA waits have eased to 6–12 weeks as mobile van fleets doubled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints are required in all filings. The CMS bone-pause code is unchanged, and private gated plans are still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the new anhedonia analyses.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: LABELLED. The Oct 2033 FDA class labeling change pools placebo-controlled trials with SHAPS or equivalent instruments: clinically meaningful anhedonia in 3.1% of incretin users versus 1.8% on placebo. Rates rise with dose, and the label cites observational rates up to ~12% at retatrutide 12 mg. Applied to ≈78.4M users, a 1.3-point excess implies ≈1.0M excess cases if causal. It usually resolves within 4–8 weeks of dose reduction or stopping. Low-dose 'calm' users show lower rates in the first independent cohort (≈2%), which vendors cite.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warnings and Precautions section with the prevalence estimate, a Medication Guide statement, and a requirement that telehealth 'calm' vendors reproduce it. No boxed warning. The FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Millions of episodes a year from gating, pauses and anhedonia stops. Cheaper restarts shorten off-periods.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users and in generic users without counselling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance and the Part D counselling screen; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The full adolescent bone dataset was submitted in Nov 2034 and is unreviewed. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; FDA review of the adolescent data is pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Down. Imports fell from 3.8M to 2.8M users as $39 legal generics undercut the risk premium. The remaining users are mostly on tirzepatide and retatrutide copies, and poison-centre calls are down about 20% from 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts continue. Individuals are still not prosecuted. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistently higher fall-related ED visits in long-term 65+ users. The absolute count rises with the band.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: DEXA cohorts confirm the pattern in users over 50 with three or more cycles.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In joint professional guidance; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean rise of several bpm at retatrutide 12 mg; the CVOT has not read out.

New entry. Pharmacist and poison-centre reports describe users moved between differently calibrated generic pens and vials, especially Medicaid users switched by formulary, who double-dose or under-dose. Mostly GI events, with some hypoglycaemia in insulin co-users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA drug safety communication (2034) on pen labelling consistency; no recall.

food_and_beverage.state: With 28.6% of adults on the drug and cheap generics reaching the bottom third, the decline has moved down-market. Dollar-store salty snack and candy volume is falling ~6% a year in the South and Midwest, faster than at mainstream grocers. A third major packaged-food group spun off its confectionery arm in 2033. Protein-fortified and 'bone-forward' lines keep growing, now including 'brain-plate' marketing aimed at cognition-indicated seniors. A small 'full-flavour' heritage segment is growing off the backlash.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of US spirits volume decline. Beer volume is falling faster in lower-income ZIP codes since generic entry. Non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' formats hold. Some bars in Atlanta and Austin market 'unmuted nights' to off-drug crowds.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down. Spend per cover is ~10–12% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls are the default. Chains' weekend 'full table' nights have become a branded backlash-adjacent product. Value buffets are now rare outside tourist corridors.

apparel.state: Size churn continues. Resale and rental sized for cycling are mainstream. Mid-market brands cut plus-size ranges again as bottom-third uptake rises, while 'unapologetic' fat-fashion labels tied to the backlash see the first growth in the segment since 2028.

fitness.state: Growing. Prescribed lifting and DEXA-plus-coaching chains are spreading. Senior 'brain and bone' classes pair strength work with cognitive-indication marketing. Staffing for older lifters remains the constraint.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is up to 71% because generic-first designs are cheap. ~70% of it is gated. Some employers add 'continuity credits' of $25–50/month in premium for 12-month PDC, operated as wellness incentives. Commercial pharmacy trend is ~+2% despite volume growth. Life insurers ask untreated BMI ≥30 applicants why. Medicare Part A fracture and fall costs keep rising off-budget from the drug.

pharma.state: US revenue falls from ≈$145B to ≈$119B while users rise 18%. Novo's US semaglutide revenue roughly halved, and it leans on amycretin and its authorised generic. Lilly is largely insulated by tirzepatide, its cognition label and retatrutide. Amgen has a monthly franchise. Indian generic makers (Dr. Reddy's, Sun, Biocon) gained a large US business, and DEXA and bone-agent makers keep winning. The decline was priced in and is not a shock.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is ordinary across classes now, so the body signals regimen quality rather than treatment. Trained shoulders and stable lean mass mean the good drug with coaching. A thin, forward-stooped frame means generic without follow-up. Visible, untroubled fat on a young person increasingly reads as a choice, and in some circles as a political one.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use levels have nearly converged (bottom 27%, top 30%), so thinness has stopped marking class. The marker has moved to which drug and how it is managed. Top-third over-50s run MariTide or retatrutide with DEXA and antiresorptives. Bottom-third users get $10 or $35 generic semaglutide, kiosk weigh-ins and formulary switches. A small, visible slice of affluent under-40s in Brooklyn, Austin and Atlanta's Old Fourth Ward are off by conviction, and being unmedicated has become a status display there.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are still the norm. The backlash has revived the deliberate feast: Atlanta 'Full Table' suppers, Tulsa congregational fellowship meals advertised as 'come hungry', and Sunday no-gram rooms whose crowds are younger than in 2032.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The on/off field on apps is now often filled 'unmuted', the backlash's word, which has gone from a niche filter to a common one among under-30s. Since the anhedonia label, people disclose dose on a second date the way they once disclosed antidepressants.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again for the first time since 2029. The backlash is now a visible coalition: fat-acceptance activists in Atlanta and Oakland, 'appetite is a gift' churches in Tulsa and Dallas, natural-health influencers, disability lawyers and some union locals. The anhedonia label gave it a shared language. Its slogan, 'feel everything', is printed on tote bags and on church signs. It is loud and growing among under-35s and Southern evangelicals, but remains a minority against 78M users.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Oct 2033: 3.1% versus 1.8% placebo in pooled trials, dose-dependent, with observational rates up to ~12% at retatrutide 12 mg. That implies ≈1.0M excess cases among ≈78.4M users if causal. The first independent cohort of ≈4.6M 'calm' subscribers suggests ≈2%, which the subscriptions advertise as 'below label'.
interior_life.framing: Treatment in the label, character in HR. Clinicians call it a labelled adverse effect. Employers never name it and talk about 'steadiness' and 'continuity'. Users still call the bad version 'the grey', and the backlash calls the whole thing 'the mute'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Institutions reward the blunted without saying so. Large employers in logistics, call centres, banking back offices and fleets run monthly on-site MariTide injection days. They pay continuity credits for 12-month PDC and include 'focus' subscriptions in lifestyle accounts. A widely cited 2034 working paper finds continuous users at Phoenix and Columbus call centres are 23% less likely to quit within a year and file fewer conflict complaints. Managers read it as a reason to promote continuity, and unions read it as evidence of selection pressure. CWA and Teamsters locals bargain 'dose sovereignty' clauses that bar using adherence data in discipline. Sales, hospitality and creative workers still dose down before peaks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' of mid-tempo pop has a counter-scene. 'Unmuted' shows in Atlanta, Nashville and Tulsa advertise off-drug performers, and audiences pledge 'no dose this week'. Streaming services tag 'written unmedicated'. Extreme sports, hot sauce and loud venues keep growing among users chasing stimulus.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Since the label, sex therapists and couples counsellors cite the prevalence figure to patients. 'Restart' packs and dose-holiday weekends are routine. A new friction is the partner whose employer credit depends on not taking the holiday.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Two arguments run side by side. Payment politics continues, focused on the 5% response threshold, which cognition-indicated seniors often miss. The body politics is new. In the 2034 midterms Georgia and Oklahoma candidates ran 'feel everything' messages against 'pharma steadiness at work', and a cross-ideological bloc of populist right, fat-acceptance left and disability advocates appeared at the same rallies. No law passed. 'Calm voter' effects are still unpublished.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA labels anhedonia with a prevalence estimate, approves MariTide and survodutide with body-composition monitoring, and grants tirzepatide a cognitive-risk indication with an explicit limitation of use. Generic semaglutide is approved under the 2031 settlements. Import enforcement remains selective with no individual prosecutions. The FTC continues to act through consent orders.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The existing Part D obesity benefit and 90% Medicaid match continue unchanged in law. Expansion came through generic pricing, $10 Part D generic tiers and eight more states adopting the existing standard (39 plus DC). No new federal or state mandate this step.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, a 5% response threshold or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, the 90-day bone pause, and a 6-month suspension after two misses. Indiana and Arkansas keep 12-month rules. The new surveillance is private: clinic-administered monthly injections give employers exact adherence records, and continuity credits run through wellness programmes. BMI-linked surcharges up to 30% continue.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets run on-site MariTide days and DEXA for drivers over 55. Army accession is still contested, and the Air Force waiver policy is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Most US generic semaglutide is finished in India from Chinese API. Generics are largely exempt from the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs, which helped the price fall and leaves the cheap tier exposed to any change in tariff policy. Lilly's new fill-finish capacity ended retatrutide allocation in 2033. Amgen's MariTide supply is US/Puerto Rico-based.

events.event: Six generic semaglutide makers and a Novo authorised generic launch under the 2031 settlements; within fifteen months cash prices fall to a median of about $39 a month and imports drop by a quarter
FDA approves Amgen's monthly MariTide with body-composition monitoring in the label; employers in logistics and call centres begin on-site monthly injection days within the year

FDA adds reward blunting to all incretin labels under Warnings and Precautions: clinically meaningful anhedonia in 3.1% of users versus 1.8% on placebo, higher at top doses; 'calm' vendors must reproduce the statement

Most Part D plans place generic semaglutide on a $10 tier, and by July eight more states, including Georgia and Missouri, adopt the existing continuation standard; Medicare and Medicaid now pay more incretin fills than employers

FDA approves tirzepatide to reduce the risk of cognitive decline in adults 60 and over with overweight and a vascular risk factor, citing a 21% relative reduction in MCI or dementia, but states it is not a treatment for Alzheimer's

A Fortune 100 logistics firm extends a $50-a-month 'continuity credit' to 140,000 workers; the same month about 40,000 people join Atlanta's 'Feel Everything' march, and the Southern Baptist Convention passes a resolution warning against 'pharmacological dulling of God-given desire' outside medical need

open_tensions: Tirzepatide's cognition indication brings seniors who are lighter at baseline into the CMS continuation standard, whose 5% response threshold was written for obesity. Many cognition-indicated users depend on clinician overrides each cycle, and the same drug that protects the brain on paper is adding to the hip-fracture count (≈16,800 excess a year).

Employers now reward continuity with on-site monthly injections, adherence data and credits, while the FDA label states that about one user in seventy-five has excess anhedonia from the drug. Unions, disability lawyers and the backlash argue this selects for the blunted. Because no state action has addressed it, it is being fought contract by contract.

The price collapse happened only for semaglutide. Public programmes are cheap at the generic tier, but the drugs with the best body-composition and cognitive claims (tirzepatide, retatrutide, MariTide) stay branded at $179–449. A two-tier pharmacology now sorts users by payer rather than by price alone.

The cheap tier depends on Indian finishing, Chinese API and a generic exemption from Section 232 tariffs. Medicaid formulary switches are producing a new dosing-error signal, and the adolescent bone data submitted in Nov 2034 is unreviewed while pediatric use climbs on $35 generics.
still_true: The CMS continuation standard's terms are unchanged from the Dec 2031 final rule: ≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weigh-ins, a 5% response threshold, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and the 90-day 'bone pause' code that private gated plans are not bound by.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still impose 12-month lockouts after two missed verifications, and the disability-rights litigation remains unresolved in the Seventh Circuit.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
Wegovy's brand list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
No US generic tirzepatide exists; Lilly's tirzepatide and retatrutide remain branded, and individuals importing pens are still not prosecuted.

prose.headline: The $39 Shot and the Monthly Clinic: America Gets Steady, and a Growing Crowd Demands to Feel Everything
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 the drug is no longer expensive, and that changes what people argue about. In March 2033 generic semaglutide arrived on the date the lawyers had set two years earlier. Within fifteen months a month's supply costs about thirty-nine dollars at a chain pharmacy and ten dollars on most Medicare plans. In a dozen Southern states it costs nothing on Medicaid. Twenty-eight or twenty-nine of every hundred American adults are on an incretin, and the gap between the richest third and the poorest has shrunk to three points. Thinness no longer tells you anything about money. What tells you about money is which drug a person is on and who checks their bones.

The cheap drug is the old one. Tirzepatide, Lilly's triple agonist and Amgen's new monthly MariTide are all still branded at between one hundred eighty and four hundred fifty dollars. They are the drugs with the better muscle data, the stronger effect and, since April, the brain. A four-year trial found that tirzepatide cut the risk of sliding into mild cognitive impairment or dementia by about a fifth in people over sixty with a vascular risk factor. The FDA approved it with a sentence saying it is not a treatment for Alzheimer's. Medicare covers it, so older Americans are now among the heaviest users. The bone problem is getting worse: on current estimates about seventeen thousand excess hip fractures a year, in a population taking the drug partly to protect their minds. Many of these new users began lean and never lose the five percent the Medicare rule demands, so every six months a doctor has to sign that they should stay on.

Most public fills are now paid by public programmes. Eight more states signed up for the federal match once their share of the generic bill fell to a few dollars a head. Medicare and Medicaid together pay for more pens than employers do. They spend less than they did in 2032, because most of their users are on the cheap molecule.

Employers, meanwhile, have found something they like. MariTide is a monthly shot, and at a logistics hub in Ohio or a call centre in Mesa it is given in a conference room on the first Tuesday by a contracted nurse. The company therefore knows exactly who came. Many pay a premium credit for a year of unbroken use. No one writes that they prefer calmer staff. A working paper found that continuous users quit less and file fewer complaints, and personnel departments quote it often. Unions now bargain over whether injection-day attendance can appear in a disciplinary file.

The same autumn the injection days spread, the FDA put the grey into every label. Clinically meaningful anhedonia occurs in about three users in a hundred, against fewer than two on placebo, and in roughly one in eight on the highest triple-agonist dose. It usually lifts within weeks of stopping. The 'calm' subscriptions now print the warning at checkout and advertise that their own rate is lower.

That number gave the opposition a shared language. Atlanta's fat-acceptance collectives, Tulsa's 'appetite is a gift' churches, the natural-health sellers and the disability lawyers now march together. In June forty thousand people walked through Midtown Atlanta under 'Feel Everything' banners, and the Southern Baptists passed a resolution against dulling God-given desire. Young people put 'unmuted' on their dating profiles. Clubs in Nashville book unmedicated acts. No law changed. The coalition is still a minority of the country, though it is a vocal one. Everyone else takes the ten-dollar pen, books the bone scan, keeps the credit and mostly feels fine.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Ortega parks at the call centre in Mesa at 6:50 and joins the line outside Conference B. It is first Tuesday. The nurse knows her name, swabs her belly and gives the MariTide shot in four seconds. A green tick appears on the badge app, and her next paycheck will show the continuity credit, fifty dollars, as it has every month since March.

She takes calls for nine hours. A man shouts about a freight charge. She feels it arrive and then flatten, like a wave on sand. Her team lead calls her a rock. She was not like this before, but she isn't sure what she was like.

At lunch she drives to her mother's. Ana is seventy-two and on Zepbound for the memory indication. It costs her fifty dollars a month on Medicare. They take the bus to the Walgreens, where the kiosk weighs her. Down 3.1 percent. The screen says CLINICIAN REVIEW REQUIRED. Marisol photographs it for Dr. Patel, who signs the override every six months and sighs about it. The DEXA van comes in nine weeks.

"Do I remember things better?" Ana asks on the ride home.

"You remembered the bus."

At seven her son Teo, nineteen, comes in wearing a FEEL EVERYTHING shirt and smelling of hot wings. He has a show in Tempe tonight, an unmuted bill. He asks if she wants to come.

She pictures it: the noise, the crowd, all of it at full volume. She would like to want to go.

"Next time," she says, and she means it, and she knows she probably won't go.
